statements.status_notes: Debian's python3-cryptography 43.0.0-3+deb13u1, the build this image ships, includes the upstream fix for the missing subgroup validation of SECT curve public keys, first released in cryptography 46.0.5. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-26007

This OpenSSL flaw in RFC 7250 raw public key handshakes affects OpenSSL 3.2, 3.3 and 3.4 (https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20250211.txt). It is reported against cryptography because the project's PyPI wheels from 42.0.0 to 44.0.0 bundle an affected OpenSSL (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-79v4-65xg-pq4g). This image ships Debian's python3-cryptography 43.0.0-3+deb13u1, which is built from source and links the system OpenSSL 3.5.7, so the bundled copy is not present.

The advisory covers the copy of OpenSSL that the cryptography project statically links into its PyPI wheels before 48.0.1 (OpenSSL advisory https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt, fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.7), and states that builds from source are not affected. This image ships cryptography built from source: Debian's python3-cryptography 43.0.0-3+deb13u1 links the system OpenSSL 3.5.7, and the Alpine py3.14-cryptography 47.0.0-r0 package links the system OpenSSL 3.5.9, so the bundled copy is not present. See https://github.com/pyca/cryptography/security/advisories/GHSA-537c-gmf6-5ccf

Upstream GCC commit 2d296e9f024edbb49cad1f3ebb5ae34c71ea5f7a rewinds the basic_filebuf put position when outputting the put area fails in overflow, so the put pointer no longer stays past epptr after a failed write. The fix is backported to Debian's gcc-14 14.2.0 source. Debian has not published a fix yet; see https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-125709

DHI backport of upstream gh-150751 (python/cpython commits 2eb2af805c156ca52b316bb4ced5e0ab3971d0ae and 9f52b443c002cccfb54bda0706a9276b6b4a109d) applied to 3.10.22 through 3.15.2. http.client validates the Content-Length header as decimal digits only (RFC 9112 1*DIGIT), ignoring optional spaces or tabs around the value; a value with a sign, an underscore, or an embedded space is not used as the body length. Chunk sizes are validated as hexadecimal digits (RFC 9112 1*HEXDIG, 0-9, a-f and A-F), so valid upper- and lower-case hex chunk sizes are accepted, while a sign, a 0x prefix, an underscore or leading whitespace is rejected instead of being parsed with int(value, 16).

Debian security tracker: fixed in unstable by the same change as CVE-2026-85091, which is upstream zlib commit df84af25dc1942490e1d1c899a07619152a46148. This package build includes an adaptation of that upstream change for the zlib 1.3.1 code base. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-76844

CVE-2026-102474 describes a heap write in the printf/echo %b Unicode \u and \U escape path in newer dash sources. Debian dash 0.5.12 (the upstream version in this package) does not implement those Unicode escapes in conv_escape; only octal and basic C escapes are supported. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-102474

CVE-2026-102473 applies to dash when built with the internal pmatch() matcher (configure --disable-fnmatch). This rebuild configures dash with --enable-fnmatch so pathname globbing uses libc fnmatch(3) instead. See https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-102473

CVE-2026-0989 is uncontrolled recursion in the RelaxNG external-schema inclusion parser, fixed upstream in libxml2 2.15.2. Alpine 3.x ships libxml2 2.13.9; backporting the RelaxNG recursion-depth fix to 2.13.x is not practical. DHI catalog images use libxml2 as a general-purpose XML library and do not document RelaxNG schema validation on untrusted RelaxNG inputs as a supported runtime path.

Both Debian (unimportant) and upstream consider this negligible. The upstream recursion-depth fix targets libxml2 2.15 catalog.c and does not apply to the 2.13.x source without invasive changes for a negligible CLI-only issue.
